title: PRD clearance corridor and signoff owners map
creator: Liam Chen
description: Purpose: Define a deterministic "clearance corridor" for PRD signoffs so every PRD change has a named owner, explicit acceptance criteria per function (Eng/Design/Legal/Security), and SLA for decisions. Scope: this ticket covers the PRD for "Structured Output v2" scope reduction (prompt/response schema changes) and the cross-team acceptance flow required for rollout to Dedicated and Private tiers. The output of this ticket will be: 1) a one-page signoff map (owners + handoff points), 2) per-team acceptance criteria checklist, 3) a decision SLA table (when to escalate to Head of Product / CTO), and 4) links to required artifacts (Confluence PRD, design mocks, threat model, evaluation harness). Why now: Recent scope drift on structured-output changes caused two missed rollouts and an unplanned hotfix; we need a lightweight but enforceable clearance path to avoid repeated delays. Success metrics: signoff latency under 5 business days for non-blocking reviews, zero unreviewed schema changes shipped to Dedicated/Private, and explicit rollback/playbook attached to PRDs. Out-of-scope: tooling implementation (automation of reminders) — that's a follow-up. Key stakeholders: Product (Aisha Verma), Eng owners (Marco Silva), Design owner (Priya Nair), Legal reviewer (Erik Holt), Security reviewer (Yvonne Park).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Every PRD change includes a mapped owner for Eng/Design/Legal/Security with contact and escalation owner
A2: A checklist attached to the PRD enumerating functional test cases, performance thresholds (latency P95), and privacy constraints
A3: Legal provides a documented clearance statement or flagged open items within 5 business days
A4: Design signoff includes annotated mocks or an accessibility exception if applicable
A5: Engineering confirms canary rollout plan, fallback model variant, and automated telemetry to detect regressions
A6: A documented rollback/playbook is linked in the PRD and validated in tabletop runbook review
